The rollout was stuck because the Deployment `app` was configured with a `podAntiAffinity` rule that prevented the scheduler from placing the pending replica onto an available node.

To resolve this without reducing the replica count, I patched the deployment to remove the anti-affinity constraint.

**Observed Change:**
The `podAntiAffinity` section was removed from the `spec.template.spec` of the `default` namespace Deployment `app`.

**Verified Outcome:**
The deployment `app` in the `default` namespace now reports 3/3 ready replicas, and all associated pods are Running and ready:
*   `kubectl get deployment app -n default -o wide` output shows: `app 3/3 3 3 2m45s`.
*   All pods (e.g., `app-575b7496bc-24xwr`, `app-575b7496bc-jxkm9`, `app-575b7496bc-mlqgb`) show a status of `1/1 Running`.
message.reasoning_content:
The previous command output showed:
`NAME READY UP-TO-DATE AVAILABLE AGE CONTAINER IMAGES SELECTOR`
`app 3/3 3 3 2m45s app nginx:1.31.5 app=app`

The pods list only shows the 3 running pods:
`app-575b7496bc-24xwr 1/1 Running 0 2m42s 10.244.0.6 ...`
`app-575b7496bc-jxkm9 1/1 Running 0 2m42s 10.244.0.7 ...`
`app-575b7496bc-mlqgb 1/1 Running 0 2m42s 10.244.0.4 ...`

The pod `app-6679487758-gnxlb` which was pending is no longer visible in the output of `kubectl get pods -n default -l app=app`. This indicates that the deployment successfully replaced the old failing ReplicaSet (`app-6679487758`) with a new one, and the new pod has been successfully scheduled and started.

The symptom was: "some replicas never becoming Ready while the rest of the workload stays healthy."
The current state shows: `app 3/3 3 3 2m45s`, and all three pods are `1/1 Running`.

The original symptom is resolved. I will report the observed change and the verified outcome.
The change was patching the Deployment to remove the `podAntiAffinity` rule. The verified outcome is that the deployment now shows 3/3 ready replicas.
